title: Migraine-prone today?
caption: Migraine-prone today? Space weather is stormy, which can make light and screens feel harsh for some. Dim screens, wear shades or a cap outside, keep lights low, and pace the day with soft tasks and short breaks.
snapshot: Geomagnetic storm conditions are active. Earth’s magnetic field is unsettled with a strong southward tilt. Solar wind speeds are typical, and no new flares or CMEs were reported.
affects: Headache and migraine sensitivity may rise, especially with bright light or long screen time. Some can feel a tight, pressurized head or a quicker build from mild to more intense. Noise and visual clutter can stack up faster than usual.
playbook:
- Dim screens and reduce glare
- Wear sunglasses or a cap outside; lower overhead lights
- Use short, eyes-closed breaks during screen blocks
- Hydrate and keep meals regular
- Keep plans flexible and quiet where possible

The background: a geomagnetic storm is active and Earth’s magnetic field is tilted southward, which tends to stir our sensory load even though solar wind speeds are only average and there aren’t fresh solar eruptions in play.

fb.caption:
Migraine-prone today? If your head feels like a dull, vise-grip pressure behind the eyes and brightness turns sharp fast, you’re not imagining it—some people may be more light- and screen-sensitive right now, and noise or visual clutter can pile on quickly. The background: a geomagnetic storm is active and Earth’s magnetic field is tilted southward, which tends to stir our sensory load even though solar wind speeds are only average and there aren’t fresh solar eruptions in play.

Make the day easier by softening inputs: set devices to their darkest comfortable settings, wear sunglasses or a brim outside, and lower overhead lights at home. Try bundling screen tasks into tidy blocks, then close your eyes for a couple of minutes to let your visual system reset; steady water and regular meals help keep the ramps from steepening. Aim for fewer moving parts—choose low-glare errands and quieter rooms so small signals don’t stack. Gaia Eyes watches how storm-tilted magnetic fields tend to line up with light-triggered headache days, and today fits that pattern.
